sections.A: The landscape point (p,d) is the binary quadratic form x^2 + pxy + dy^2 (its values at (1,a) are the rate V(a)). Its even Clifford algebra is spanned by 1 and theta = uv with theta^2 = p theta - d, which is the theta-lift; the landscape law is the geometric product of two lifts, read as a ratio. The circle operation's form x(x+y) is split.
sections.B: Exact match: the sign of p^2 - 4d picks C (circle), split-complex (line) or dual numbers (border). The circle operation (1,0) is the split case in the idempotent coordinate theta = (1+e)/2; its wall -1 is the zero divisor 1 - theta (the light cone); conjugation is the inverse.
sections.C: Brennan's 'k as a fused number': with scalar arguments, any multivector dial K that satisfies a quadratic gives a landscape law with p = trace(K), d = norm(K). The circle operation's own k is a null (light-cone) multivector k(1+e)/2. Curvature is minus the square of K's non-scalar part. A general K in Cl(3,0) gives the landscape over the complex numbers 1 and I (the volume element).
sections.D: Kept: associativity, identity 0, the lift (the gr-bridges sandwich law). Lost: commutativity; the commutator of two vectors is twice their oriented area. Kept information: giving each factor its own direction stores every subset product on its own blade (2^n parts); the ordinary circle operation is the scalar shadow that adds them up. The wall becomes a set: two points, none, or a cone.
sections.E: Bott's mod-8 pattern carries over through the shift X -> 1 + X unchanged (the circle-operation monoid on Cl(p,q) is a copy of its multiplicative monoid), so nothing new there. What the shift adds is a classification of the wall: it stays the single point -1 exactly in the three division algebras R, C, H (Cl(0,0), Cl(0,1), Cl(0,2)); in every other Cl(p,q) a blade squares to +1 and the wall grows into a cone of zero divisors shifted to -1.
sections.F: Existing analog made exact: twisted boosts' half-velocities are rotor charts. tan(phi/2) composes by the circle law, tanh(phi/2) by velocity addition. The chart (the law's value) cannot tell R from -R; the lift 1 + a theta keeps the sign.
sections.G: Existing (twisted boosts): the d=+1 dial boost is a unit-direction quaternion; its product's scalar part is 1 - u·v and its i-part is the wedge u×v. Grassmann's exterior product is the antisymmetric part of the corner (section D: x✳y - y✳x = 2 x∧y).
sections.H: Exact: Clifford's ω with ω^2 = +1, 0, -1 (elliptic, Euclidean, hyperbolic space) is one of our three 2D algebras, chosen by the sign of space curvature, just as the dial's d sets curvature K = d in the twist rule. The circle operation's idempotent theta is Clifford's elliptic projector (1+ω)/2, the piece that splits a motion of S^3 into its left and right parts. Naming caution: the elliptic case uses the split ring.
sections.I: Dual-number arguments turn the circle operation into its first jet (cf. the jets page). Border-country laws are re-charted dual numbers.
sections.J: Exact: the twist rule's corner phase arg(X+iY) is half the triangle's area on the d=+1 sphere, which is the holonomy of the Hopf fibration, whose fibres are Clifford parallels. The same circle |t| = 1 is the light wall at d = -1 and the base of the Clifford torus at d = +1.
sections.K: Partial: the circle law's group is already a circle (its ruler arctan is periodic), its finite subgroups tan(pi j/n) are 1-D Clifford–Klein forms, and the chart is the quotient S^3 -> elliptic space. No higher-dimensional circle-operation form (flat torus built from ✳) yet; it would need two commuting dials (a 2-parameter group) and a lattice in it.
sections.L: Holds by transfer only: landscape translations are Möbius maps, so Clifford's chain theorem survives in every chart, with lines becoming circles through the image of infinity. No circle-operation statement of the chain itself; it would need concurrency written as a ✳ identity (real cross-ratios).
